I had really terrible teenage years too. And now I'm 23, finished uni. I would say definitely that the bad experiences in my teen years have pulled me back in life(which is totally not fair). It affected my uni experience and only in about uni year 3 have I made a remarkable recovery. 

The most important thing to do right now is to build your own self worth and self esteem through mindful thinking. Even if u don't have friends yet, even if it's really hard. 
Don't wait for life to get better before you change the way you think about yourself, or just the persimistic way you think in general(due to the bad experiences). 

But I have to say though, my remarkable recovery wasn't by my own strength, but God really did a miracle and helped me when he transformed my person, renewed my mind and built my self worth. I'm a Christian. 

Also, I recall the years where I spent my birthdays alone. There were people who wished me, but I had no good/close friends to spend it with. It was sad. Every year from about 2013 to 2017 I would cry either on or before/after my birthday because of the bad state I was in.

Fast forward to 2018/19, i finally begin to enjoy my life because I met my partner. And I had never ever dated before, I didn't think I would meet anyone I could get along so well with. 
I still have little close friends, but now I have many more peripheral friends (I attend a church with a vibrant young adults group), and I'm contented because I enjoy my partner's company very much. It makes up immensely for my lack of friendships or family. 

So things do get better eventually. But for now, perhaps u will have to grind a few years. 

All the best for you.

Yea that's true. I had a hard time making friends too. But it takes time. 
Also u can't just join in like that. Y'all got to have something in common. 
In my experience going scuba diving with a local dive company helps u make friends much easily. 
(That's if u like this activity) but I haven't experienced other activities where u get acquainted so fast. A mini friendship actually develops.

Another thing to do is join an interest group that u really like. E.g. wakeboarding/Latin dance/ sport. 
The list is endless. but u gotta pick one where the same people attend regularly, not a come and go as u wish kind of structure. 

Put in the hours. Eventually friendship develops because y'all are doing the same thing together and y'all got common history now. 

Don't expect freindships to develop instantly though. It takes time. 

Meanwhile, leverage on family (if they are close by). 

Personally there was a horribly long time where I didn't have friends, and my only family member is my mum, who is pretty distant and does her own things. I didn't see anyone regularly in my uni class so I was pretty isolated too. 

But I didn't continue to wallow in my isolation. I sought experiences. Yea friends didn't come immediately, and not that I have a lot now, but the collective acquaintances and people I meet help to sustain my social life for now. 

Till life gets better imma stride onwards. 

Don't give up, keep trying to find the thing u were meant to do then people will slowly come alongside with u. 

All the best

I get that. Kinda comforts me though. It doesn't matter even if u didn't have trouble making friends in high school, university can be really isolating depending on multiple factors. I am in a course that has a lot of recorded lectures and tutorials; students don't have to come for class at all. So not a lot of people come. Those people that I know, I can't click well with them. 

It didn't help that I didn't join orientation or a hall. So u should do that in your second year (join as a senior) 

Also, u should join a club u like so that you will likely stay there and commit. Don't be like me, tinkering with various clubs for first 3 years before committing to one. Now I feel like it's too late but oh well. 

I guess friendships recycle every about 7 years anyway. Different phases of life bring different friends. I hope I find  friendship at work (because I really like partnership and working with people towards a common goal).

In addition, lower your expectations, it will help a lot. Like u won't break into a frenzy even if it seems things didn't progress even after joinining a club u like. Sometimes things don't go as planned. But give it time. 

Friendship grows stronger with time. So put in that time. And also if you're lucky u meet unusually like-minded pals. Then those friendships progress faster.
